subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw implement provider-capacity blocked prompts as a core SQLite-backed durable queue/replay path, and which overlapping PR or workstream should become canonical?
rationale: The remaining work crosses provider fallback, session suspension, channel delivery, and persistent queue ownership, and the repository policy rules out ad hoc runtime sidecars while several open PRs propose partial approaches.

options.title: Approve one SQLite-backed core design
options.body: Make this issue the canonical product/architecture target and require overlapping PRs to converge on one durable queue, replay, and visible-status contract.

options.title: Land only bounded mitigations
options.body: Accept narrower fixes such as restart follow-up persistence or quota cooldowns while keeping the broader capacity-wait replay behavior uncommitted.

options.title: Reject durable replay
options.body: Keep provider exhaustion as a surfaced failure or suspension state and require users or clients to prompt again after capacity returns.

recommendation.title: Approve one SQLite-backed core design
recommendation.body: Make this issue the canonical product/architecture target and require overlapping PRs to converge on one durable queue, replay, and visible-status contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent queue lifecycle work plus adjacent suspension history make this the best available owner signal for the product boundary choice.
